items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:59:1
items.html:
Hesed, and the vessel broke and fell into Bina of Beria, and the light came down to the vessel of Yesod of Atzilut, since the light of Daat had already preceded to take the place of Malchut: The explanation is that at the time when the lights are clothed in the vessels, it is regarded that whichever is coarser than its fellow is greater than its fellow, for the one whose screen is coarser brings out a greater level, as is known. However, at the time when the vessels are empty of lights, their coarseness is then regarded as a deficiency, and therefore it is regarded the other way around: that whichever is more refined is the more important.
And this is what he says: “And the vessel of Hesed fell into Bina of Beria.” For the vessel of Daat is drawn from a coupling on a screen of phase four in conjunction with phase three, as above (page 517, the passage beginning “The Daat”), while the vessel of Hesed is drawn from a coupling on phase three alone. Thus the vessel of Hesed is found to be more refined than the vessel of Daat, and therefore the vessel of Hesed is regarded as being above the vessel of Daat, meaning that it is more important than it because it is more refined; understand this. And this is what he says: “And the light came down to the place of the vessel of Yesod,” for according to the value of the vessels, so is the value of the records that clothe in them, and therefore the records too are regarded according to the importance of the vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:59:2
items.html: Gevura, and it broke, and the vessel fell into Hochma of Beria: That is, as above, that whichever is more refined than its fellow is more important than its fellow, since after the departure of the light from the vessels the coarseness is regarded as lowliness. In the same way, the vessel of Tifferet is even more important than the vessel of Gevura, and therefore it fell into Keter of Beria. Thus the four vessels — Daat, Hesed, Gevura and Tifferet — fell into KHBD of Beria, which are the GAR of Beria, just as the vessels of HGT were the GAR of ZON. However, they fell in the reverse of their degree, that is, Daat below them all, since it is the coarsest of them all and therefore its breaking is the harshest of them all; less than it is the vessel of Hesed, which is only from phase three of coarseness; and less still is the vessel of Gevura, which is only from phase two of coarseness; and the vessel of Tifferet, whose breaking is the least of them all, since it is only from phase one of coarseness. In the same way the records of the vessels fell: the record of Daat in Malchut of Atzilut, that is, below them all, at the Sium of Atzilut; and above her, Hesed, in Yesod of Atzilut; and above her, Gevura, in Netzah and Hod of Atzilut; and above them all, Tifferet, which remained in its place, that is, in Tifferet of Atzilut — all according to the relation of the vessels.

Of NH of Atzilut, which are the two flanks of the Guf: This is only while they are in the phase of posterior, lacking the illumination of Hochma; but when they are in the phase of anterior, that is, when there is in them the illumination of Hochma, they are then counted as two Sefirot distinct from one another.
The reason for this you will find above in the words of the ARI (page 332, item 42, and page 333, item 43), where he brings that the Sefira of Netzah is drawn from the VAK of Keter, which is then Lo Mati [not reaching] in Hochma, and therefore Netzah is regarded as having no illumination of GAR of Hochma in it, while the Sefira of Hod is drawn from the phase of Mati [reaching] in Hochma, and therefore Hod is regarded as having the illumination of Hochma shining in it. See there and in the Inner Light. Thus the entire distinction between Netzah and Hod lies in the illumination of Hochma, which is absent in Netzah and present in Hod. Now, this difference is possible at a time when there is illumination of Hochma in the Partzuf as a whole; but at a time when there is nothing in the illumination of the Partzuf as a whole except the illumination of the posterior of Ima, there is then no longer any difference at all between Netzah and Hod, since in Hod too there is no illumination of Hochma, just as in Netzah, and therefore they are then counted as a single Sefira. Accordingly, the Sefirot Netzah and Hod of Nekudim, which have in them only from phase two of YESHSUT, and which are also clothed in the posterior that fell from the upper AVI, as above, and in which there is no illumination of Hochma — they are therefore counted as a single Sefira.
And one should not ask that according to this the Sefirot of Hesed and Gevura, too, ought to be counted as a single vessel, since the entire distinction between Hesed and Gevura was explained there to be likewise in the illumination of Hochma, which is present in Hesed and absent in Gevura. For the difference between HG and NH is great. This is because the force of the posterior of Bina begins essentially, in all the Partzufim, only from Bina downward, for the reason that every phase nurses from the phase that corresponds to it in the ten Sefirot of direct light. And since this posterior is not included at all in the two Sefirot Keter and Hochma, but only in Bina, therefore in Hesed and Gevura too, which are the phase of Keter and Hochma of the Hassadim, as is known, the force of the posterior does not act upon their own phase with respect to themselves; rather, from Tifferet downward, which stands in the relation of Bina, as is known, the posterior acts in its full measure. Therefore Hesed is always regarded, even at the time of the Katnut [smallness] of the Partzuf, as including GAR, which is not so with Gevura, and you have a great difference between Hesed and Gevura: for Hesed with respect to itself in any case includes GAR, unlike Gevura, which is in the posterior over the GAR from its root.
